If you’re looking around Coventry, I’d start with **The Royal Kennel Club’s puppy-finder** rather than buying from a general classified ad. Its current Staffordshire Bull Terrier listings include blue puppies, although availability changes quickly. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

Locally, you could also contact Brazen Kennels in Berkswell and The Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club in Cannock. I’d treat these as leads to investigate rather than endorsements of any particular breeder.

[royalkennelclub.com](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What to ask the breeder

For a Staffy, **health testing should matter more than the fact that the puppy is blue**. Blue is an accepted Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour under the current breed standard. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/breed-standards/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

Ask these questions:

- **Can I see the mother with the puppies?** Ideally meet the puppies where they were raised, not at a car park or unrelated address.
- **Can I see the father's details and health-test results too?**
- **Have both parents been DNA tested for L-2-HGA and hereditary cataracts (HC-HSF4)?**
- **Have the parents had the recommended eye and elbow examinations?** These are among the Royal Kennel Club's recommended Staffy health tests. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/BreedSpecificRequirements?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **What are the parents' hip/elbow scores and eye-test results?** Ask to see the actual certificates/results rather than accepting “fully health tested” as an answer.
- **What is the parents' inbreeding coefficient (COI)?** Ask for the individual parents' registered names so you can check their records yourself.
- **Have there been allergies, skin problems, neurological problems, eye problems or other significant illnesses in the parents or close relatives?**
- **How have the puppies been socialised?** Ask specifically about people, household noises, handling, other dogs and normal home experiences. Early socialisation is particularly important for Staffies. [PDSA](https://www.pdsa.org.uk/pet-help-and-advice/looking-after-your-pet/puppies-dogs/medium-dogs/staffordshire-bull-terrier?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **What vaccinations, microchipping and worming have been done?**
- **What food are they eating, and what routine are they used to?**
- **What happens if I develop a serious problem with the puppy after purchase?** A responsible breeder should have a clear contract and be willing to take the dog back if necessary.
- **Can I take my time and come back for a second visit?** Pressure to pay a deposit immediately is a warning sign.

### Particularly important with a "blue" Staffy

Be cautious if the breeder is heavily marketing the puppy as a **rare/fashionable colour**, charging a large premium specifically for blue, or breeding primarily for colour. The Royal Kennel Club explicitly advises that health and temperament should take priority over colour and warns about health considerations associated with fashionable-colour breeding. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/your-dog/getting-a-dog/are-you-ready/rare-and-unusual-colours/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

Also, don't accept “KC registered” as equivalent to “health tested.” Registration by itself doesn't establish that the parents have had all the appropriate health screening.

If you tell me **how far you're willing to travel from Coventry (e.g. 30, 60 or 100 miles)** and whether you want a **male or female**, I can search current listings and narrow them down to breeders where the parents' health information is publicly verifiable.
